jobs.objective:
Write Burrow, one protocol for Squeekchain on Ethereum Sepolia where a Squeek NFT can be collateral, a marketplace and a Uniswap v4 hook both pay their fees to the same vault, and bonding sells discounted shares for assets the treasury keeps. Foundry, unit tests plus Sepolia fork tests, and a deployment script the operator runs. Do not deploy from the job.

The vault share token is named Burrow SQK, symbol bSQK, 18 decimals. Holding bSQK is the single way to earn from everything: loan interest, marketplace fees and swap fees all arrive as SQK into the vault and raise the share price. There is no rebase and no second staking contract.

LIVE ADDRESSES, every one verified by calling it; pass them to constructors, never hardcode. SQK 0x5501e1fa81be1c3f49225fa7668da0245d07db60, ERC20 with EIP-2612 permit, 18 decimals. Squeek NFT 0xcb98349c134ab983da5bfd80527dfe2552bdb70f, ERC721, 9987 minted. Squeekchain staking 0x4b67b739dfd832f4eac67a7aa3bc244fb74cea4f exposing deposit(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), withdraw(address collection, uint256[] tokenIds), claim(address recipient), setClaimRecipient(address), claimable(address) view, basePower(address account, uint8 collection) view, accountPower(address) view, stakeOf(address) view, stake(uint256), unstake(uint256 amount, uint256 maxFee, uint64 deadline) returns (uint256 net), quoteUnstake(address,uint256) view, exitPolicy() view returning (uint16 minBps, uint16 maxBps, uint16 saturationBps, uint8 windowDays, uint256 pressureFloor), live value (200, 6000, 2000, 7, 21000000e18). Uniswap v4 PoolManager 0xE03A1074c86CFeDd5C142C4F04F1a1536e203543, PositionManager 0x429ba70129df741B2Ca2a85BC3A2a3328e5c09b4, Permit2 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3. The public Squeekchain docs are stale for this deployment: their claimable(uint8,uint256[]) and position(uint8,uint256) selectors revert here, so call no signature this objective has not listed.

1. BurrowValuer. creditLine(uint256[] tokenIds) view returns the SQK a borrower may owe, equal to summed NFT power times pricePerPower times ltvBps over 10000. Power per level comes from a table set at construction matching the published policy 1000, 3000, 7000, 15000, 31000, 63000 and upward. There is no NFT market on this chain so pricePerPower is governed and is the main attack surface: the owner may move it only through a two day timelock, by at most 20 percent per change, inside a hard band fixed at construction. ltvBps capped at 6000. Events on proposal and execution with old and new values.

2. BurrowVault, ERC20 bSQK, the lending core and the single fee sink.
Lenders: deposit(uint256 assets) mints shares against totalAssets, which is idle SQK plus principal outstanding plus accrued interest. withdraw(uint256 shares) burns and pays from idle SQK, with a clear custom error when utilisation leaves none.
Borrowers: openPosition(uint256[] tokenIds) pulls NFTs with safeTransferFrom, records each level, then calls staking.deposit and staking.setClaimRecipient so the collateral keeps earning for the vault. borrow(uint256 amount) requires debt plus amount at or below the valuer line. repay, repayAll and closePosition, which calls staking.withdraw and returns the NFTs once debt is zero. Interest is a fixed per second rate set at construction, capped at 50 percent a year, accrued on every touch.
Self repaying loans, the heart of this: sweepRewards() calls staking.claim for the vault and applies what arrives first to accrued interest, pro rata by each position's escrowed power, then to principal. While the hamster runs, the loans shrink by themselves. Anyone may call it.
Liquidation: when debt exceeds the line, liquidate(address borrower) lets anyone repay the debt and take the NFTs, with liquidationBonusBps capped at 1500, surplus recorded for the borrower. Liquidation reverts within one hour of a price change so governance cannot harvest borrowers.
Fee sink: donate(uint256 amount) pulls SQK and raises the share price without minting. The marketplace and the hook call it. Nothing else is needed to pay stakers.
Bonding: bond(address asset, uint256 amountOrId, uint256 minShares) accepts a Squeek NFT or a v4 SQK pool position, values an NFT through the valuer and a position through its SQK principal, mints bSQK worth that value plus bondDiscountBps capped at 2000, vesting linearly over bondVestingDays, claimable with claimBond(). Bonded assets stay in the treasury; bonded NFTs are staked so they earn.

3. BurrowMarket. list(uint256 tokenId, uint256 price), cancel, buy with SQK pulled from the buyer, and a Dutch auction used for liquidated NFTs that decays linearly from a premium to a floor over a fixed window. Every sale takes feeBps, capped at 500, and forwards it with vault.donate. Sellers are paid the rest in the same transaction.

4. BurrowHook, a Uniswap v4 hook for the SQK pool, built on BaseHook from v4-periphery against the PoolManager above. Permissions: afterSwap and afterSwapReturnDelta only, declared in getHookPermissions. In afterSwap, when the output currency is SQK, skim hookFeeBps capped at 100 of the output, take it from the PoolManager with poolManager.take, and forward it with vault.donate; when SQK is not the output currency, take nothing. A v4 hook only works if its address carries its permission bits, so the deployment script must mine a CREATE2 salt with HookMiner and deploy through the deterministic deployer, and a test must assert the deployed address has exactly the declared flags.

RULES. Solidity 0.8.26, OpenZeppelin for ERC20, ERC721Holder, SafeERC20, ReentrancyGuard and Ownable2Step, v4-core and v4-periphery for the hook. Every value moving external function nonReentrant, checks effects interactions. Custom errors only. Token id arrays capped at 32, strictly ascending, no duplicates. The owner has no path to user assets: the only powers are pausing new borrows, the timelocked price, and parameters inside their hard caps.

TESTS. Unit tests on a mock staking contract mirroring the real one: share price never falls on deposit or withdraw, borrow refused above the line, interest accrual, sweepRewards cutting debt, liquidation one wei either side of the boundary, the timelock rejecting early or oversized moves, the post move liquidation freeze, bond vesting and discount caps, marketplace fee routing into the share price, hook flags matching its address, and every custom error. Fork tests with vm.createSelectFork pinned to a Sepolia block, deal for SQK, vm.prank on a real Squeek holder, proving against the real deployed staking and NFT contracts a full round trip: escrow, still earning, borrow, sweep, repay, close. Invariants: total assets never fall except on withdrawal, and summed debt never exceeds summed credit lines. Ship script/Deploy.s.sol reading the live addresses and parameters from environment variables, mining the hook salt, deploying all four and wiring them, plus a README with every address, every assumption, the unaudited testnet only warning, and the exact forge commands.

jobs.objective: Launch two contracts in this repository on Robinhood Chain, in this order, without changing their logic. 1) src/ConditionalsV2.sol:ConditionalsV2, constructor (address owner = $owner, IERC20 imd = 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, IIntake intake = 0xa43e6f75ee006411f79ac1c84120606c2330de82, address oracleSigner = 0x5598aa9146215bc13eb26f2c692ad1461fd32982, address feeRecipient = 0x63bcf2d1483c7628d7d53704ff9c8199dc28d907). 2) src/ConditionalsZap.sol:ConditionalsZap, constructor (ConditionalsV2 conditionals = $contract:ConditionalsV2, IPoolManager poolManager = 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951, IERC20 imd = 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, IERC20 usdg = 0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168). Neither constructor makes external calls. ConditionalsV2 is a conditional prediction market in IMD settled by the IdentityMD oracle. A market asks 'if CONDITION, will OUTCOME?' with four outcomes (index 2*world+side). A share of the outcome that happens pays 1 IMD. The creator deposits two 0.5 IMD oracle questions plus a neutral seed of b ln 4 that funds an LMSR maker (0.5 to 100 IMD b, Solady expWad and lnWad, log-sum-exp, rounding margins that keep makerBalance >= C(q) >= every q[i]); the seed is the creator's maximum loss. Until closeTime: stakeConditional (and stakeFor, paid by the caller and credited to an account) mints a complete set, sells the opposite side to the maker and buys more of the chosen side, so the stake is paid in its world on its side and refunded in the other world; buy, sell and exit trade with the maker with slippage bounds. Every maker trade pays 2%: half accrues to the creator in owed, 67/200 is sent to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD because IMD reverts on transfers to zero, and the rest accrues to feeRecipient in owed. When the maker is short of every outcome it turns those complete sets back into IMD (_absorb). The oracle flow is unchanged from Conditionals v1, IMD launch 2278, audited: after resolveTime anyone calls requestResolution, the contract pays the Intake with requestWithFailure for oracle.request@oracle-1 questions (panel 5, quorum 4, bool, panel evidence, window pinned to one Ethereum block, block.number - 10, since block.number on Robinhood Chain is the Ethereum block number) and stores keccak256 of each canonical question document. onOracleResult (selector 0x510379c7) accepts an answer only from the Intake for its own pending request, with the stored questionHash, answerType bool, panelSize and quorum at least the market's, agreed >= quorum, not expired, and an EIP-712 signature (domain IdentityMD Oracle, version 2) from the market's oracle signer. onFailure (0x5a0df71e) only clears the ask. Settlement pays 1 IMD per share of the outcome that happened and gives the creator the maker's residual and unspent budget. With no usable answer 30 days after resolveTime anyone can void: accounts get their net IMD in back excluding fees, pro rata if short, and the creator is paid last. The owner can only propose an oracle configuration for future markets behind a 3 day delay and set the fee recipient; it cannot touch trades, answers or open markets. No token, no proxy, no pause. ConditionalsZap has no owner and holds nothing between calls. stakeWithEth and stakeWithUsdg swap exact input through two hookless Uniswap v4 pools (USDG to ETH, fee 500, spacing 10; ETH to IMD, fee 10000, spacing 100) inside one PoolManager unlock, revert on a partial fill or below the caller's minImd, and call stakeFor for the caller. All positions, exits and payouts are in IMD in ConditionalsV2. ConditionalsV2's runtime is close to the 24,576 byte limit with optimizer_runs 1, so any fix must keep it under. legacy/ holds the deployed v1 for reference and is not built. The test suite (unit, fuzz, invariant, oracle conformance vector and a live-API question-hash vector; fork tests with FORK_ROBINHOOD=1) must keep passing.

Squeek Dome — IMD Job Brief
Full spec: https://github.com/0xtakoyaki22/squeek-dome
Goal: one-page, non-custodial Squeek holder + Keeper workbench on Sepolia. Any visitor can crank; an owner can batch-claim and merge. Real transactions only.
Scope: Sepolia only, chain 11155111 / 0xaa36a7, testnet assets have no value. No new contract, staking, or minting (minting paused). Use only exact values below. Reads via https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com, so page works before wallet connects. window.ethereum only for connect, chain switch, eth_sendTransaction.
Contracts
SqueekCore V3: 0x74665dAecA35A2303e767E76a2FF1FB6F93e119f
SqueekMining V6: 0x3beE588fC20dE788Bac17d33b41Da7346cb27EC4
SqueekNFT: 0x0eAF3E0d40A0a8E5a6Ac030b2459E9FB0B7905c6
DotGrid: 0x2dC7661D172fEf0FC900E0aD0f4ffCE68E8bfD75 (via tokenURI only)
Collection always 0. REWARD_PER_BLOCK Sepolia is 5,600 SQK (6,900 is launch). Block height = cumulativeBlockUnits / 1,000,000,000 (= blockHeight in Core.state()).
Exact functions
SqueekMining:
checkpoint() — permissionless, pays Sepolia gas, no reward. Call checkpointStatus() first.
checkpointStatus() returns (bool corePaused, uint64 nextRound, bool roundSettled)
state() returns 13 fields in this order: (uint256 minted, paid, totalWeight, rewardIndex, uint64 closedThroughBlock, lastActivationRound, uint256 weightActivationCursor, weightActivationCount, bool bootstrapped, uint64 processedThroughRound, closedCumulativeWork, uint96 closedCumulativeBlockUnits, uint32 closedWorkPerThousandBlocks). Pending = count - cursor. Query weightActivation only for cursor .. min(count, cursor+32)-1; if cursor==count, query none.
weightActivation(uint256 index) returns (uint64 round, uint192 addedWeight)
position(uint8, uint256) returns (uint64 activeWeight, pendingWeight, uint40 pendingRound, uint48 nextMergeBlock, uint8 level, uint256 lastIndex, accruedScaled). Level 0 = burned/unminted, no revert. pendingRound != 0 = cannot merge. accruedScaled is SQK x 2^128, NOT 18-decimal SQK — use claimable() for unclaimed SQK.
claimable(uint8, uint256[]) returns uint256, 18-decimal SQK claim would pay now. There is NO function called previewClaim. It needs 1-32 IDs, strictly ascending, no duplicates, but does NOT check ownership.
claim(uint8, uint256[]) — owner only, 1-32 IDs, strictly ascending, no duplicates, else InvalidClaim. Fraction stays on lowest ID.
merge(uint8, survivorId, donorId) — owner only, both owned by caller, distinct, same level 1-9 (max 10), pendingRound == 0, nextMergeBlock <= SqueekCore blockHeight. Donor burned permanently. Survivor +1 level, keeps ID/image and both credits.
SqueekCore state() returns 8 fields in this order: (uint64 settledThroughRound, cumulativeWork, uint96 cumulativeBlockUnits, uint64 blockHeight, uint96 blockProgress, uint32 workPerThousandBlocks, uint256 authorizationNonce, bool paused). Use settledThroughRound as frontier, blockHeight for merge checks. Do NOT use a version with workPerThousandBlocks before blockHeight, or genesis/lastSettlement timestamps — not in CoreState.
SqueekNFT: ownerOf(uint256), tokenURI(uint256). NOT ERC721Enumerable: tokenOfOwnerByIndex does NOT exist, never call it. Images: tokenURI -> decode base64 JSON -> render image field (inline SVG) as isolated image, never inject into markup. ownerOf/tokenURI REVERT for burned/unminted IDs — scans must catch reverts and skip, not crash.
IDs and ownership
Load IDs by: (a) user-typed IDs or RPC scan 1..30 via ownerOf, skipping reverts, (b) 1-click "Load Live Sepolia Sample Holder" scanning ownerOf 1..20 until an address owns >=2 live Squeeks, then scanning its IDs, (c) OPTIONAL API api.squeekchain.com/v1/owners/{address}/squeeks — unconfirmed, never depend on it.
STRICT: API is display only. Never take ID, amount, owner or eligibility from API into a transaction. Re-verify every candidate via RPC: ownerOf, position, claimable. Operators CANNOT claim/merge — only direct ownerOf can.
Panels (one top bar, one shared state)
Panel 1 — Keeper Crank (works with 0 Squeeks): show checkpointStatus + Mining state (processedThroughRound, totalWeight, minted, paid, pending count) + up to 32 waiting activations, vs settledThroughRound. Buttons: "Simulate Checkpoint (eth_call)" showing OK or exact decoded revert; "Crank Checkpoint (Send Tx)" only when corePaused==false and roundSettled==true. When roundSettled==false, keep Simulate active and state sending now would revert and waste gas — never present force-send as success. After receipt, link tx hash and re-read status/state. No manual roundSettled toggle — state only from RPC.
Panel 2 — Batch Claimer: connected wallet OR pasted/sample holder in Inspect Mode (Send only if connected wallet owns every selected ID). Table: ID, thumbnail, level, activeWeight, pending round, nextMergeBlock, unclaimed SQK from claimable(0,[id]). Select 1-32, auto-sort ascending, dedupe, reject level 0 / unowned. Show batch claimable(0,sortedIds), highlight lowest ID keeping fraction, simulate, then send claim(0,sortedIds).
Panel 3 — Merge Arena: only eligible pairs (distinct, same level, pendingRound==0 both, nextMergeBlock<=blockHeight both). Side-by-side images, level, activeWeight, combined unclaimed SQK. Swap toggle must instantly re-render BOTH cards, SQK amounts, combined total, and modal IDs; a swap changing only hidden dialog values is a FAIL. "Prepare Merge" opens a blocking modal naming BOTH IDs: "Token #DONOR will be BURNED PERMANENTLY and cannot be restored. Token #SURVIVOR will advance one level, keep its ID/image, and inherit both credits." Only after a confirmation checkbox, simulate, then send merge(0,survivorId,donorId).
Transaction wiring
Check eth_chainId == 0xaa36a7, switch if wrong. Real eth_call to Mining, then eth_sendTransaction with from, to=Mining, data, value 0x0. Wait for receipt, link https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/{hash}. No setTimeout fakes. Decode reverts with Mining errors (RoundNotSettled, CorePaused, InvalidClaim, InvalidPosition, InvalidMerge, Unauthorized); if undecodable, fall back to checkpointStatus, never raw hex alone.
Acceptance (all must pass): 1. Real calldata + eth_call + chain check + eth_sendTransaction, no mocks. 2. Unconnected Inspect Mode via public RPC, incl. 1-click sample holder. 3. 0-Squeek wallet can simulate Panel 1 and, when roundSettled, send checkpoint(). 4. Out-of-order claim IDs auto-sort; duplicates/unowned blocked. 5. Merge cannot send without burn modal naming both IDs. 6. Desktop + mobile; at 375px top bar wraps, no truncation/scroll to buttons.
Out of scope: custom contract, staking, minting, prediction markets, games, leaderboards, bots, music, art, simulator-only buttons.

Produce ONE test edition of Open Interest's daily crypto-discourse brief through the paper's full pipeline: three independent drafts, one selection, one adversarial review. The edition spec that every draft must follow in full:

Produce today's TEST EDITION of a daily crypto-discourse brief. Plain text
only, under 900 words total. This is a drafting rehearsal: quality of voice
and sourcing is the entire point.

FIRST: fetch and obey the house style guide at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openinterest-ai/paper/main/style-guide.html
Its rules are binding: declarative sentences, numbers with context, no banned
words (delve, landscape, game-changer, seamless, robust, unlock, tapestry,
paradigm, "it's worth noting", "ever-evolving", emoji), at most one em dash
in the whole edition, absolute dates only, no financial advice.

SOURCES: open platforms only (Farcaster, research blogs, Mirror, Substack,
governance forums, GitHub; X only via open mirrors). Prefer the last 24-48
hours. A claim that cannot be verified against an open-platform source is
cut, and the cut is noted in METHOD. When sources conflict on a figure,
prefer the primary source; otherwise state the range and attribute both.
Cite with the full source URL in square brackets; for these plain-text test
editions this overrides the style guide's numbered-citation example.

STRUCTURE (exactly):
LEAD: a headline (short declarative sentence ending in a full stop), a
2-sentence deck, then 150-250 words. Every factual claim carries a source
URL in brackets.
ALSO TODAY: exactly three items: category tag, one-sentence headline with
full stop, 2-3 sentence summary, at least one source URL each.
READING LIST: 3-5 links, each with a 1-line reason.
METHOD: one closing paragraph: sources swept, hours covered, any items cut
for failed verification and any claims resting on secondary sources.

ACCEPTANCE: the structure above, complete; every claim sourced; under 900
words; no banned words; headlines are declarative sentences with full stops;
absolute dates only (no 'this week', 'yesterday', 'the weekend'); at most
one em dash in the whole edition.

CONTINUITY: before drafting, fetch https://openinterest-ai.github.io/paper/rehearsal.html and the prior test editions linked there. Do NOT lead with a story a prior edition led with unless a material NEW development happened after that edition published; an ongoing story without a new development may appear only in ALSO TODAY, and only with the new angle stated.

jobs.objective:
# Squeek Sprouts — IMD objective (paste into explorer.imd.fun/launch)

Build "Squeek Sprouts": a single-page, static, browser idle-farming game for Squeekchain where crops grow ONLY from the real wheel work of Squeektoshi, the hamster that powers Squeekchain. It is a game people play and come back to, not a dashboard.

## Core idea
- The player owns a 3x3 pixel-art garden. Each crop needs a fixed amount of "wheel work" (wheel passes counted by Squeekchain) to ripen.
- Growth = currentCumulativeWork - workWhenPlanted. When the hamster naps, the garden sleeps (night scene). When he runs, it grows, even while the player is away (idle game).
- Harvesting while the hamster is running is a "fresh harvest": 2x crumbs and a 15% chance of a GOLDEN crop worth 5x.

## Live data (public, CORS-enabled, no key)
- Poll `GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/status` every 15 s.
  - `measurement.cumulativeWorkUnits` (string number): the growth counter.
  - `measurement.counterEpoch`: if it changes, or the counter goes down, rebase every planted crop so it keeps the progress it had (planted = newWork - (lastWork - planted)).
  - `measurement.coreStatus` (`SPINNING` | `IDLE`), `rpmMilli` (/1000 = RPM), `speedMmPerSecond`, `distanceMm`, `freshness` (`online` or stale; if not online show "signal stale, garden paused" and do not count it as running).
  - `builder.projected.blockHeight`: show as Squeek block height.
- Optional fallback: if the API fails twice, switch to a clearly labelled DEMO wheel (simulated naps/runs, separate save slot) so the page never looks broken.

## Economy (keep these numbers)
| Crop | Work to ripen | Seed cost | Sells for | Unlocks after crumbs earned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheel Radish | 40 | free | 6 | 0 |
| Zoomie Carrot | 120 | 8 | 20 | 30 |
| Round Pumpkin | 400 | 30 | 70 | 150 |
| Rim Sunflower | 1000 | 90 | 190 | 500 |
| Moon Melon | 3000 | 260 | 600 | 1500 |
- Start with 10 crumbs and 3 open plots. Plots 4–9 cost 25, 60, 120, 250, 500, 1000 crumbs.
- Save state in localStorage (wrap in try/catch). A "Reset garden" button needs two taps (no confirm() dialogs).

## Screens and feel
- Left panel: a pixel-art canvas of Squeektoshi on his wheel. The wheel spins at a speed scaled from the live RPM; the hamster bobs when running and sleeps with "zzz" under a moon when idle. Below it: status pill (RUNNING · GROWING / NAPPING · GARDEN SLEEPS / STALE / DEMO), work counter, RPM, speed (m/s), distance (km), block height, and "work grown here".
- Main panel: seed shed (each seed shows its pixel sprite, cost, work needed, price, or lock state), the 3x3 garden (tap empty plot = plant selected seed, tap growing plot = shows work left, tap ripe plot = harvest, tap locked plot = buy), progress bars, a glowing border on ripe crops.
- Garden journal: timestamped log of ripe crops, harvests, golden crops, unlocks, counter restarts.
- All crop sprites are drawn on canvas in code (4 growth stages each, distinct ripe shapes: radish, carrot, pumpkin, sunflower, crescent-marked moon melon). No emoji, no stock images. Fonts: Silkscreen + VT323 from Google Fonts. Warm dark palette (soil browns, leaf greens, gold accent).
- Must work on phones (garden stays 3 columns, panels stack).

## Stretch (only if cheap and safe)
- "Sign in with wallet" via a signed message (no gas, no approvals) to show the player's short address on a local high-score card. Never request transactions or token approvals.

## Delivery
- Pure static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no backend, no private keys, no transactions.
- Host on IPFS/ENS and deliver the code to GitHub. README explains the data source and the growth/rebase math.
- Footer: "Reads Squeekchain's public API. No wallet, no gas, nothing is signed."

Revision to the existing website only. Do not redeploy or modify the contract, its address, the ABI or the deployment config (imd-deployment.json). Keep all current behaviour, layout, styling and data reads unchanged.

1. RENAME. The project is now called "Squeek's First Road Trip" (replacing "Hamster Road Trip"). Update it everywhere visible: page title, loading text, header wordmark, hero and section text, help text, meta and Open Graph/Twitter titles and descriptions, the share image (share.svg), favicon labels, README and docs. Deliverables: (1) a smart contract on Sepolia, (2) a website, (3) the full source code of both published on GitHub in a public repository, (4) the website hosted on IPFS.

PROJECT
Hamster Road Trip is a community game. The real Squeekchain hamster's wheel distance moves a marker across a world map, starting at Miami Beach, Florida. The community votes on where the hamster travels next. The hamster does the walking and the community chooses the route.

HOW THE GAME WORKS
1. The game runs in 24-hour epochs. During an epoch, each wallet votes once for one destination from a fixed list of 64 destinations (ids 0 to 63).
2. When an epoch ends, the destination with the most votes wins (ties go to the lowest id) and is added to the end of the route queue.
3. The marker travels to the first destination in the queue, then the next, and so on. Progress is driven only by the hamster: distance travelled = real wheel km x SCALE, where SCALE is one config value (default 100) shown on screen.
4. If the queue is empty or the wheel is idle, the hamster rests (sleeping animation and a short story line) and waits.
5. Arriving at a stop shows a postcard: place name, a one-line fun fact and a pixel-art icon. Every arrival is added to a trip log.
6. A Navigator leaderboard ranks wallets by how many of their votes matched winning destinations.

Constructor takes epochSeconds (86400) and destinationCount (64). vote(destinationId): one vote per wallet per epoch, rejects ids out of range. finalize(epoch): callable by anyone once the epoch has ended, records the winner once. Views: currentEpoch, votesFor(epoch, id), winnerOf(epoch), hasVoted(epoch, wallet). Events for votes and finalization. No owner, admin, upgrade path, token or payments. STRATOKS — FIX VISITOR AUTHENTICATION DELIVERY BEFORE PRODUCTION

Repair the existing delivery from job a5886b35-7174-42da-9056-421ecd5001df. Base: https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-2725-stratoks-restore-wallet at 4671102884260ac798821bd32bfad7f462aacf7f. Preserve the current Expanse world and walletless viewing. This is source, frontend preview and owner-run backend delivery; do not access or deploy to production.

1. RECOVERABLE SESSION CHECKS
shared/visitor-auth-client.js currently destroys a valid session and queues logout on any refresh error. Retain the credential on 429, 5xx, offline and timeout, show a temporary unverified/unavailable state, and retry with bounded backoff/jitter and Retry-After support. Only an authoritative invalid-session response ends that session. Never represent an unconfirmed session as freshly verified. Explicit logout and account/network/provider/world changes must still clear obsolete auth immediately and revoke safely. Prevent stale responses and duplicate refreshes; preserve retry/cancel flows.

2. PROXY-AWARE RATE LIMITS
The server keys all visitors on the Caddy connection IP; about 30 tabs exhaust the shared 60/min bucket. Add explicit owner-configured trusted proxies and correct client address extraction ONLY through that trust boundary. Ignore forged forwarded headers from untrusted peers; document Caddy header sanitization and private backend binding. Separate bounded challenge/verify abuse limits from authenticated session polling. Keep global/body/concurrency limits. Test 50 verified sessions behind a trusted proxy polling at the shipped cadence while another visitor signs in; no false expiration or unfair shared-IP lockout.

3. BOUNDED PROFILES AND SESSIONS WITHOUT PERMANENT LOCKOUT
Throwaway addresses currently fill the durable 10,000-profile store forever; one signer can consume all 2,000 sessions. Add a documented bounded retention/admission policy that recovers at capacity, with per-peer/time signup controls and expiry/eviction of inactive records as appropriate. Do not promise Sybil-proof identity. Preserve retained profiles atomically across restart and disclose retention. Bound active sessions per address and origin; new sessions cannot monopolize capacity. Test small configured limits, many distinct disposable signers, repeated one-signer sessions, expiry and restart recovery. Never silently erase world or resident memory.

4. SIGNED MESSAGE AND CANCELLATION
Validate world identity against the actual server's structured format, not an assumed UUID (existing world IDs may be world-20260101-0). Reject control characters/newlines and malformed fields in world/domain/origin/URI before opening a wallet prompt; reconstruct and verify the exact server-issued message. Keep address/chain/origin/world/nonce/expiry binding and replay protection. Publicly displayed nonce must not be a revocation credential for an established session. Use a separate unpredictable cancellation secret or an equivalently secure design to cancel late verification without introducing account-switch races. test cancellation before/during/after verification and wrong-secret/origin attempts.

5. REPRODUCIBLE DEPLOYMENT
Fix Docker COPY ownership/permissions so USER node can read modules even from umask 077 checkouts. Run import checks as that runtime user; retain shared/ modules. Provide correct Expanse Caddy/compose routing on 8788, including /api/auth/*, /api/expanse/* and static assets; remove legacy 8787 guidance. Explicit AUTH_URI/origin configuration, private profile volume, backup and rollback instructions. Build AND start linux/arm64 image on native ARM or documented emulation; probe health/config and disposable-signer login/logout.

6. UI AND REGRESSIONS
Remove repeated unavailable-backend copy and duplicate screen-reader status announcements. Preserve EIP-6963 provider choice, legacy fallback, current HUD, inspector, camera and mobile controls. Separate wallet connection from server authentication. No approvals, transfers, contracts, paid gameplay or new token. Preserve population, identities, brain weights, goals, signals, terrain, schema and live configuration. Demo must remain clearly labelled.

DELIVER AND PROVE
Add regression tests reproducing each defect before the fix and passing after. Run existing backend/client/typecheck/build suites and real HTTP crypto tests. Exercise browser login/logout, transient failures, account/network switch races, 320/390px mobile layout and anonymous viewing with disposable signers; distinguish simulated providers from actual extensions/devices. Verify copied-world load/save/restart without changing simulation behavior. Publish updated source and static preview, API/setup/rollback docs, raw test evidence and a finding-to-fix matrix with commit/file/test references. List unresolved issues explicitly; accepted task status alone is not evidence they are fixed.
